title: The Falcon
paragraphs: Detective adventures centered on Michael Waring, known as the Falcon, who investigates murders and other crimes in a long-running series that changed lead actors and formats over time.
Detective series centered on Michael Waring, the radio Falcon. The radio Waring lineage derives from Drexel Drake and should not be collapsed into the separate RKO film Falcon identity.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Blue Network / Berry Kroeger (April 10, 1943 to December 18, 1943) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], Mutual / James Meighan (November 27, 1945 to July 3, 1947) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Les Tremayne era (July 10, 1947 to May 7, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC/Kraft / Les Damon (May 14, 1950 to July 5, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Les Damon (performer), Drexel Drake (creator), Ed Herlihy (announcer), Bernard L. Schubert (producer and transcriber), Richard Lewis (director), Arlo (music), and Eugene Wang (writer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].
The stories often return to private investigation, murder and homicide, fraud and deception, and robbery and theft.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Distinct Falcon source lineages, Postwar private-eye radio culture, and Kraft-sponsored NBC era.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|gang-busters|Gang Busters]], and [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]].
